text.text_excerpt: I went here on a recommendation from a former NOLA native. She likes food but is not a foodie. In fact she rarely remembers the name of a restaurant, so I was kind of surprised she knew the name so I figured I should go on my business trip. I got there after the dinner rush (or I assume since it was empty on a Monday night at 8pm during the summer). I got the surf & turf po' boy & a side of fries. The sandwich came with Zapp's Crawtaters, but I didn't feel like chips even though I do love me some Zapp's. The sandwich was pretty delicious and it was fresh (heard them frying up the shrimp since the restaurant was empty and quiet). The french bread on the sandwich was fresh and perfect (some...

First night in NOLA, right off the plane, and we were looking for an affordable dinner we didn't have dress up or line up for. And while the prices for burgers and sandwiches aren't on the low end, otherwise Somethin' Else fit the bill. The riverside end of Conti is fairly quiet, and there were only a couple of other tables occupied. It's a small, cozy place and the waitress was very friendly; it made for a warm welcome back to town. It was a tough decision between the Popeye salad (basically spinach and seafood) and the Shrimp Burger, which the menu claimed to be a local favorite. I went with the burger, and it was really good. Almost didn't stop here but were enticed in by the menu. Loved their eclectic selection of local breakfast items like crawfish biscuits and such. I got their chicken biscuit and LOVED it (flaky biscuit, spicy chicken, tasty sausage gravy) and my husband ordered the trio omelette with fresh crab, shrimp, and monterey jack cheese topped with a fried fish fillet on top-- he enjoyed his, too. We also ordered a boudin ball and it was so-so, but an experience. Our service was so-so. The food was worth it though.
